In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the violation of CP invariance is not due to an entropy increase, and, in turn, the entropy increase is not due to CP invariance violation.
the weak interaction is not a thermodynamic irreversible process.
the violation of CP symmetry in the weak sector of Standard Model is not a consequence of the second law of the thermodynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the violation of CP symmetry is a purely quantum phenomenon.
the quantum superposition of the same type quarks, generated in the weak interactions, cannot be considered as a source of entropy, and, therefore, cannot be related to any irreversible process.
the violation of CP symmetry is a consequence of the unitarity of Cabibbo-Kabayashi-Maskawamatrix, while the violation of T symmetry is due to the noncommutativity of quark fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum superposition of quarks is a fundamental feature of the Standard Model, which should be taken into account in the study of the CP violation in the weak interactions.
the quantum superpositions of same-type quark states generated by the Cabibo-Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix are the only ones allowed by the Standard Model.

, if we consider a quantum statistical approach to the weak interaction and the associated density matrices, we are led to conclude that the CP and T violation is not related to a thermodynamical effect.
